I've been working this land for 45 years. My father farmed before me. I know this soil. Quzhou land is flat, the well is reliable, and wheat-maize is what every family around me does — I see no reason to change what works.

My children do some factory work in the city, which helps cover the household costs. But I still need the grain. Two crops a year off 10.7 mu. That's the plan every year.

**Wheat (October planting):**
I'll rotary-till after I pull the maize in October, mix in base fertilizer — diammonium phosphate and some potash — before seeding. I use the improved variety from the supply shop in town, the one most people in the village are buying. I seed it in early October. Come March, when the green starts returning, I'll put down a urea topdressing. Irrigation: I always do four — the winter water before it freezes to protect the roots, then again at green-up, jointing, and heading. I spray herbicide in late autumn, and if I see rust spots in spring I'll spray again. Two pesticide runs is usually enough.

**Maize (June planting):**
Right after wheat harvest — maybe a day or two rest — I rotary-till and get the maize in. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer at the market has that year, it's all hybrid now. I put fertilizer down at planting and again at jointing. Summer rain helps some, so I irrigate three times: at planting if the ground is dry, at tasseling, and during grain fill. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide early, one for corn borer when I start seeing the moths.

I don't expect to change much. Prices are uncertain, inputs cost more each year, but I know how to get a decent harvest from this soil.
